I've been trying to lucid dream for six months and I've only had two, the second one happening last night. I'm currently reading Stephen LaBerge's book "Exploring the World of Lucid Dreaming" and there's a technique I read about called autosuggestion. It's essentially just completely relaxing every muscle in your body before you go to sleep and then thinking about the possibility of having a lucid dream very soon. The key is you can't think about it too hard, and it has to be the last thing on your mind before you fall asleep. Well, I don't know if this particular dream was triggered by that technique, but I don't think it's purely coincidence. When I did the reality test in the dream and figured out that I was dreaming, I stabilized myself several times, which I found was really helpful. The dream was much more vivid and lasted a lot longer than my first. I've also read about how it's pretty hard to have sex in a lucid dream, but I had sex with the first pretty girl I saw and it was very intense and I didn't wake up from it. I think it helped that I stabilized one more time before I had sex with her and I took several deep breaths to calm myself down. Afterwards though, it felt as real as when I'm awake. I roamed around a bit after that, and then tried to spawn Adolf Hitler because I wanted to talk to him out of morbid curiosity, but it didn't work. I remember "waking up" to what I thought was "reality", but it was actually just another dream. If I would have just done another reality check upon awakening, I could have had two lucid dreams in a row.

tl;dr... The autosuggestion technique triggered a lucid dream, and after I stabilized, the dream was pretty vivid and lasted a long time. Always do reality check right when you wake up, because you could just be in another dream. Also, "Exploring the World of Lucid Dreaming" is a very helpful book.
